prompt:
Normalise the single contact block in the user's note. Recognise label variants and colon, equals or tab separators in any line order. Use only record lines, never surrounding notes, signatures, email domains or company suffixes as sources of inferred values. Return only a bare JSON object with exactly name, phone, email, company, country; each value is a string or JSON null.

Trim values and collapse whitespace runs to one space. Absent, empty or case-insensitive -, --, n/a, na, none, unknown, ?, null, TBD means null. Never guess; only the international-phone country rule below can fill missing data.

Assign email to the value containing @ and phone to the value with at least seven digits and only digits, spaces or + - ( ) . / after stripping leading tel: and trailing extensions of the form ext., ext, x, # or extension followed by digits. Ignore labels for these two assignments. Use the country line for explicit country. Take name and company by label unless the name value ends in a listed legal suffix and the company value does not, in which case swap them.

• Country: uppercase ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 from an English, Swedish or German name, alpha-2 or alpha-3 code, or common alias, case-insensitively. UK/Great Britain → GB, Holland → NL, USA/U.S.A. → US, Türkiye → TR, Czech Republic → CZ.
• Phone: after stripping tel: and the extension, + or 00 at the start (ignoring an opening parenthesis) means international. Change 00 to +, remove (0) and strip spaces, dashes, dots, slashes and parentheses. Keep the written code even if it disagrees with the explicit country. If country is absent, empty or a placeholder, fill it from the international code only if uniquely assigned; shared codes such as +1 and +7 leave it null. For national numbers, strip formatting and one leading trunk 0, then prepend + and the normalised country's calling code; without country return null for the national phone. All non-null phones are E.164: + followed by calling-code and national-significant-number digits only.
• Name: move First before Last by splitting Last, First at the first comma. Drop leading Dr, Mr, Mrs, Ms, Mx, Prof, case-insensitively with or without a dot. Uppercase the first character and lowercase the rest of each space- or hyphen-separated part. Preserve Unicode letters and diacritics without transliteration; comparison is after NFC.
• Company: strip one trailing suffix and optional preceding comma, case-insensitively: AB, GmbH, AG, Ltd, Ltd., PLC, Inc, Inc., LLC, Corp, Corp., AS, ASA, Oy, Oyj, A/S, ApS, SA, SAS, B.V., N.V., S.p.A., Sp. z o.o., K.K., Pty Ltd, Ltda. Uppercase the first character and lowercase the rest of each space-separated word.
• Email: remove a mailto: prefix and surrounding angle brackets, then lowercase the entire address.
